title: Typed-chunk anchoring and disconnect eviction policy for streamed structured outputs
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: When streaming structured outputs (JSON blocks, typed tool/call events) across the wire we frequently emit partial chunks that are not valid standalone units. Client disconnects or slow consumers can leave the system holding partial KV/cache prefixes and ephemeral outputs that are hard to reconcile. In the presence of function/tool-calls, the server may have triggered side-effects (prefetches, external tool invocations) but never delivered a clear completion record to the client. This ticket defines a new "typed-chunk anchoring" model and an eviction policy that: 1) anchors eviction tombstones at typed chunk boundaries, 2) ensures function-call completion handoff or compensating actions within a bounded grace window, and 3) exposes a compatibility shim for older SDKs that expect atomic, non-chunked messages.
acceptance_criteria:
- Anchor tombstones at the last completed typed chunk; no tombstone should split a typed element across a boundary.
- After client disconnect, KV/prefix-cache and ephemeral output linked to a request are reclaimed within the configured grace window (default 30s) unless an active resume token exists.
- Function/tool-calls started during a generation must have one of: successful completion + delivery, queued compensating action, or a recorded compensating tombstone with metadata.
- Backpressure quotas enforce per-session token holdback; if exceeded, system emits a structured 'holdback' event to compatible clients and a legacy 'partial-evicted' event to older SDKs.
- Metrics are emitted: stale_chunk_count, anchored_eviction_rate, resume_success_rate, functioncall_grace_timeouts.
- End-to-end test covers disconnect during a multi-chunk function call (simulate streaming + tool call) and verifies deterministic cleanup and metrics.
implementation_notes:
Design:
- Typed chunk: a server-side boundary where the stream contains a self-contained typed element (eg. a complete JSON object, a completed function call event, or a tool call response chunk). Producers must prefer emitting chunk boundaries at payload type boundaries where possible.
- Tombstones: store minimal metadata (request_id, last_chunk_index, chunk_type, resume_token if any, eviction_deadline). Tombstone anchoring guarantees that replays/resumes can discover the logical chunk start.
- Holdback window: per-request adjustable; default 30s. During this window we keep KV cache and ephemeral outputs in a 'soft-evict' state. After window, hard eviction runs a compensating workflow for tool-calls.
- Compatibility shim: if client advertises sdk_version < 3.0, server emits legacy partial messages: a combined 'partial' event with a deterministic delimiter and an accompanying tombstone header. New clients receive structured typed-chunk events and resumable tokens.
- Rate limiting: introduce per-session backpressure credits (tokens) which are decremented for each emitted chunk and refunded on resume/delivery. Credits are quota-backed and expose an API to clients for introspection.
- Storage: tombstones kept in fast metadata store with TTL = holdback + safety margin (default 2 minutes).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'typed_chunk_anchoring' in runtime. 2) Canary on dedicated infra for 1% of traffic with short-lived prompts exercising function calls. 3) Monitor anchored_eviction_rate, resume_success_rate, and increase to 10% after 72h. 4) Enable compatibility shim for older SDK apps for 2 weeks, gather error reports. 5) Full rollout after metrics stable and no regression in latency SLOs.
- Rollout notes: coordinate with SDK team for a client release that consumes typed-chunk resume tokens and honors holdback events.
- Kill-switch: revert feature flag per-region within console.
test_plan:
Unit tests:
- tombstone serialization/deserialization across chunk boundaries.
- holdback timer transitions and hard-evict path.
Integration tests:
- simulate slow consumer that disconnects mid-toolcall; assert compensating action executed and tombstone metadata present.
- compatibility mode: older SDK receives legacy partial event; new SDK receives typed-chunk events and successfully resumes.
- load test: verify per-session credit system prevents head-of-line blocking under synthetic high-concurrency.
- chaos: induce random client disconnects and assert no more than 0.1% leak of ephemeral KV after TTL.
Observability:
- dashboards for stale_chunk_count, anchored_eviction_rate, holdback_window_violations, resume_success_rate.
- alert: anchored_eviction_rate > 1% for 10m triggers pager.
